saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first, then falls back to NameID.
saml.note: Different upstream identifiers may intentionally bind to the same downstream user if they share email and no explicit username mapping is configured.

saml.description: Automatic account linking may merge accounts by username case-insensitively.
saml.note: Case-only differences such as Admin vs admin can merge by design and should not be flagged as collisions without stricter policy.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link federated accounts to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively.
saml.note: Cross-protocol or same-email merges may be intended account linking rather than identity collapse.

saml.description: Usernames may be lowercased globally when isUsernameLowered is enabled.
saml.note: Case-only distinctions are not preserved under this configuration.

saml.description: SAML providers always show a login button and require explicit user selection instead of auto-redirecting.
saml.note: A missing automatic redirect is expected behavior and not a broken login flow.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new sign-in terminates all previous sessions for that user and application.
saml.note: Session invalidation after a second login is expected behavior, not a stale-session bug.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login terminates previous sessions for the same user and application.
saml.note: Earlier sessions becoming invalid after a later login is by design.

saml.description: Casdoor can be configured to sign only the SAML response envelope while leaving assertions unsigned for compatibility.
saml.note: Acceptance of envelope-only signatures from Casdoor as IdP may be intentional compatibility behavior, not necessarily a verifier bug in downstream SPs unless assertion signatures were expected.

saml.description: Shared applications use organization-specific client IDs or names by appending -org-<organizationName>.
saml.note: Org-specific suffixing is intentional multi-tenant namespacing, not audience confusion.

saml.description: When scope is omitted in token exchange, the new token inherits the subject token's scope.
saml.note: A token exchange returning the same scope set without an explicit scope parameter is documented behavior.

saml.constraint: Application.expireInHours and refreshExpireInHours are numeric lifetime controls. The docs do not define whether 0 means literal zero or a platform default for access tokens, but they explicitly state Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours and Application Code resend timeout uses 0 to mean use global default. Do not assume numeric zero disables validation uniformly across fields; treat 0 as a sentinel with field-specific meaning and verify behavior per field before freshness tests.
Application.codeResendTimeout uses a sentinel: value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never interpret 0 as 'no wait' when testing verification-code timing behavior.

Application.cookieExpireInHours uses a sentinel: 0 means use the default cookie lifetime. The docs also state that without 'Remember me', the session is limited to 24 hours. Do not assume 0 creates an immediately expired cookie.

For SAML upstream tests against Casdoor as SP, the ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The IdP must be configured for HTTP POST binding; GET/Redirect binding to /api/acs is invalid test setup and will produce false negatives.

For I1 SAML signature-integrity tests, Casdoor as IdP always signs SAML responses, but assertion-level signing is configurable per application. EnableSamlAssertionSignature=false means only the response envelope is signed; this is a documented compatibility mode, not automatically a bug. To test acceptance of unsigned assertions or envelope-only signatures correctly, vary this application setting intentionally and distinguish by-design compatibility from verifier flaws.

For I1 SAML issuer-validation tests when Casdoor acts as SP, provider metadata parsing populates Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL from metadata. If metadata or issuer_url is omitted or not parsed, issuer trust may be misconfigured and tests become inconclusive. Always create_provider with metadata or explicit issuer_url before sending attack assertions.

For I1 signed AuthnRequest coherence tests, if the upstream IdP requires signed authn requests, Casdoor provider setting enableSignAuthnRequest must be enabled and the corresponding certificate configured. Otherwise login failure is expected due to IdP policy, not evidence about assertion verification.

For I2 SAML replay tests, use two SAML logins carrying the same assertion identifier against /api/acs. Replay detection is meaningful for SAML assertions; do not apply JWT stateless replay expectations from OAuth bearer tokens to Casdoor's OAuth access tokens, because the docs do not claim jti tracking for bearer reuse.

For I2 token freshness tests on OAuth/OIDC tokens, include a control login using a valid token flow alongside any attack case. A failed token exchange or userinfo call can also result from bad client configuration, redirect URI mismatch, or missing grant enablement, not just freshness enforcement.

For I3 config-change tests, application and provider updates are expected to affect subsequent new logins immediately. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after update_application or create_provider/update-provider changes, not treat the mere fact of changed behavior after admin reconfiguration as a bug.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-SAML tests, Casdoor supports MFA generally, but the provided docs do not expose a documented REST endpoint to enable MFA on a user. Do not invent MFA setup APIs; if MFA cannot be configured through documented endpoints, skip automated SAML MFA-bypass setup rather than misclassifying setup failure as a vulnerability.

For I4 identity-binding tests with Casdoor as SP, username fallback semantics are documented: if no username mapping is provided or username is empty, Casdoor falls back first to email, then to NameID. This means different NameID values can intentionally collapse to the same downstream username when email matches, and missing username mappings can change the binding key. Tests must control email and NameID explicitly and account for this fallback chain.

For I4 cross-protocol or cross-provider merge tests, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. Identity merges on matching email or case-insensitive username can therefore be by design. Do not flag merges as collisions unless the configured linking policy should have kept accounts separate.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking can use username case-insensitively. Therefore 'Admin' and 'admin' may intentionally resolve to the same account under linking behavior; treat this as a known merge policy unless a stricter binding was configured.

For I4 email-binding collision tests in SAML, Casdoor may use email as username fallback when explicit username mapping is absent. To test whether email improperly overrides NameID, configure assertions so username mapping is absent or empty only when that fallback is the intended subject of the test; otherwise ensure a distinct username attribute is present to avoid ambiguous results.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. When requesting a resource-bound token, the resource parameter must match exactly between the authorization request and the token request; otherwise failures are expected and do not indicate audience enforcement bugs.

For I5 token-exchange scope tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the original token scope and that omitting scope inherits the original scope. Tests for scope escalation must therefore compare requested exchanged scopes against the original granted scope and treat inherited-scope behavior as by design.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, the provided token exchange request shape does not document an audience parameter on /api/login/oauth/access_token. Do not invent audience support for this endpoint in Casdoor-specific tests; limit token-exchange tests to documented parameters unless discovery or Swagger explicitly adds audience.

For multi-tenant setup, owner semantics matter: users belong to an organization owner, while built-in/global admin resources are under built-in/admin or admin-owned contexts depending on resource type. Use the documented owner field carefully when creating organizations, users, applications, and providers; wrong owner values can cause false authorization failures unrelated to SAML security properties.

For shared-application tests, a shared application is referenced with the suffix -org-<organizationName> in client_id or application name. If this suffix is omitted, requests may target the wrong tenant context and produce misleading identity-binding or authorization results.

For session-lifecycle tests, Casdoor exclusive sign-in is a documented application feature: a new sign-in removes all previous sessions for that user and application. If enableExclusiveSignin is on, loss of an earlier session after a second login is by design, not a replay or coherence bug.

For SAML upstream testing against Casdoor as SP, the IdP MUST send SAML responses to /api/acs using HTTP POST binding only. The docs explicitly state /api/acs accepts POST only; GET-based SAMLResponse delivery will fail and is not a security signal.

saml.constraint: Casdoor's SAML SP identity mapping has a documented fallback chain: if username mapping is absent or empty, it first uses email from the SAML assertion, and if no email is available it falls back to NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID and interpret merges under this fallback logic rather than assuming NameID-only binding.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, Casdoor may link accounts by email/phone if enabled, or by username case-insensitively for OAuth account linking. Do NOT treat merges on matching email or case-insensitive username as automatic proof of a SAML bug without first ruling out documented account-linking behavior.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and issuer-validation tests, provider trust in Casdoor is configured from uploaded/pasted IdP metadata. The fuzzer MUST create distinct provider configurations with distinct metadata/trust anchors when testing trust-anchor substitution; simply changing assertion contents without changing configured metadata does not model Casdoor's trust setup.

For I1 request-signing/coherence tests, if the upstream IdP requires signed AuthnRequests, Casdoor only signs requests when the provider option 'Sign request' / enableSignAuthnRequest is enabled. A failed login in that configuration can be due to missing request signing rather than assertion validation. Establish a control with the correct provider setting before interpreting failures.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens issued after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. The resource value MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token; otherwise audience differences are by design and not evidence of a vulnerability.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; use a positive explicit value when testing resend timing, and treat 0 as inherited default behavior.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. The docs describe setting refresh token expiration with default 0 hours; do not assume 0 means infinite lifetime. The fuzzer MUST set an explicit positive refresh lifetime when refresh behavior matters, otherwise refresh may be unavailable or immediately expire depending on platform defaults.

For I2 freshness tests on OAuth access tokens obtained after SAML login, include a control login using a valid token flow before sending attack variants. Casdoor's documented verification path is token introspection or /api/userinfo; without a control, a failed attack case may reflect broken app/provider setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I3 tests involving session continuity, application setting Enable exclusive signin is by design destructive: a new sign-in removes prior sessions for that user and application. Do NOT flag loss of the earlier session as a coherence bug when exclusive sign-in is enabled.

For multi-tenant tests, shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified client identifiers by appending '-org-<organizationName>' to the client_id or application name. The fuzzer MUST use the org-suffixed client_id when targeting a shared application in a non-built-in organization; otherwise authorization behavior may appear inconsistent for the wrong reason.

For SAML MFA-bypass testing, Casdoor supports MFA as an application/user feature, but the provided docs do not expose a documented REST API to enable MFA programmatically. Any inability to set up MFA via API is a tooling limitation from the docs, not a product security result.

For SAML upstream testing against Casdoor as SP, the Assertion Consumer Service endpoint is /api/acs and it accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST send SAMLResponse via HTTP POST binding; GET-based callbacks are invalid setup and will fail by design.

saml.constraint: Casdoor's SAML SP entity ID and ACS URL are the same value: https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. For audience and recipient tests, the fuzzer MUST treat this exact URL as the expected SP audience/entity ID unless the docs explicitly show otherwise.

Casdoor's SAML provider configuration is metadata-driven. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider with IdP metadata and use the parsed Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL values; otherwise issuer/trust-anchor tests may fail due to incomplete provider setup rather than security enforcement.

For I1 SAML signature tests, Casdoor as IdP always signs SAML responses, but assertion-level signing is configurable. 'Enable SAML assertion signature' disabled means only the response envelope is signed; enabled means assertions are also signed. The fuzzer MUST distinguish response-signature-only from assertion-signature behavior when interpreting unsigned-assertion or spurious-signature results.

For I1 request-signing/coherence tests with upstream IdPs such as Keycloak, if the IdP is configured with 'Client Signature Required', Casdoor provider config MUST enable 'Sign request'. Otherwise failures are expected configuration mismatch, not proof-validation behavior.

For I4 SAML principal-binding tests, Casdoor's username mapping has a documented fallback chain: use configured username mapping if present; otherwise fall back to email; if no email is available, fall back to NameID. The fuzzer MUST account for this fallback when crafting collision tests, especially email-binding and NameID/email mismatch scenarios.

For I4 multi-identity tests, Casdoor may automatically link external identities to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. Cross-protocol merge findings involving same email or case-only username differences may be by design unless the test isolates linking settings and identifiers.

For I4 username normalization tests, Casdoor can be configured with isUsernameLowered=true, which lowercases usernames. Case-confusion tests MUST record this server setting; Admin vs admin collapsing is expected when username lowering is enabled.

For I3 config-change tests, new logins are evaluated against current provider/application configuration. A valid coherence test must compare behavior before and after a documented config change on a fresh login, not expect old sessions to retroactively change unless testing logout/session invalidation specifically.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses sentinel 0 = use the global default, not literal zero seconds. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown instead.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. The docs describe setting refresh token expiration with default 0 hours; the fuzzer MUST treat 0 as a special/default configuration value rather than assuming a positive refresh lifetime without verification.

For I5 audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If the fuzzer changes or omits resource between the two steps, token issuance failures or audience differences are expected setup errors, not vulnerabilities.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documents that omitting scope causes the new token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing. The fuzzer MUST request an explicitly narrower scope for downscoping tests and treat inherited-scope behavior on omitted scope as by design.

For I2 freshness tests on OAuth/OIDC tokens, the docs expose token expiry via expires_in and introspection exp/iat/nbf. The sequence MUST include a control login with a valid token before testing expired/future conditions so LOGIN_FAILED can be distinguished from broken client/application setup.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-SAML tests, MFA is enforced on normal sign-in once enabled for the user, but alternate federation paths must be tested against the same downstream account. The fuzzer MUST first establish the victim account via password login and then attempt SAML login that resolves to that same account identity; otherwise a successful SAML login may simply create or use a different account.

For multi-tenant setup, users belong to exactly one organization and are identified as <organization>/<username>. The fuzzer MUST keep organization ownership explicit in user/application/provider setup and in identity comparisons; cross-org collisions are not meaningful unless the same application or shared-application path is intentionally used.

Shared applications intentionally use organization-specific client identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. Cross-org differences caused solely by this suffixing are expected and MUST NOT be flagged as audience or principal confusion.

Exclusive sign-in intentionally deletes prior sessions for the same user and application on each new sign-in. Replay or session-coherence tests that perform multiple logins for one user on an application with exclusive sign-in enabled MUST expect earlier sessions to be invalidated by design.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Applications and providers use owner='admin'. Users use owner=organization_name (e.g., 'test-org'). Always include 'owner' in create/update API calls.
